input: Set up a dedicated creative studio space in the spare room

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of creative work (painting, music, photography, writing, crafts, etc.) completely determines what equipment, layout, and infrastructure are needed.
Whether the space is for one person or shared by multiple people (or a mix of disciplines) affects storage, layout zones, and how the room is organised.
The current state of the room — empty, cluttered, used for storage — determines how much clearing and prep work comes first.
The available budget directly shapes whether this is a DIY/budget build or involves purchasing new furniture, equipment, acoustic panels, lighting rigs, etc.
Knowing the desired timeline (weekend project vs. phased over months) shapes how the tasks are sequenced and prioritised.
Atmosphere and aesthetic priorities (inspiring vs. minimal, mood lighting vs. bright daylight, industrial vs. cosy) drive furniture and decor choices significantly.
Understanding what 'done' looks like — the first creative session held, a fully fitted-out room, or something in between — sets the finish line for the whole plan.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a creative studio in the spare room
gold.taskDescription: Transform an existing spare room into a functional, dedicated creative studio space.

questions.title: What type of creative work will this studio be used for?
questions.description: Identify the primary discipline(s) — e.g. painting, music production, photography, writing, crafts — as this determines every major setup decision.

questions.title: Will this space be used by just you, or others too?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo studio or shared by multiple people or disciplines, which affects layout zones and storage needs.

questions.title: What is the room's current state — empty, furnished, or cluttered?
questions.description: Understand how much clearing, cleaning, or prep work is needed before the setup phase can begin.

questions.title: What is your overall budget for this project?
questions.description: Determine the financial envelope — e.g. under £500, £500–£2,000, or no firm limit — to guide furniture, equipment, and finishing choices.

questions.title: When do you want the studio to be ready to use?
questions.description: Establish the target completion timeframe — a specific weekend, a few weeks, or a phased multi-month build — to sequence tasks accordingly.

questions.title: What atmosphere or aesthetic do you want the space to have?
questions.description: Capture style and mood preferences — e.g. bright and minimal, warm and inspiring, industrial, or gallery-like — to guide decor and lighting decisions.

questions.title: What would make this setup feel like a complete success to you?
questions.description: Define the finish line — whether that is holding the first creative session, having every item in place, or reaching a specific functional milestone.
